title: [Chapitre] I. Vers une géométrie des formes (topologiques) : notes manuscrites (05/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp.17-19). Grothendieck is studying 1-dimensional combinatorial 'models' of a regular (topological) form: (quasi-)ordered sets L that are connected, 'regular' (every element has strictly bigger and strictly smaller elements, a' < a < a'') and 'locally strictly increasing/decreasing'. They are tested against axioms F1-F5 defined earlier in the chapter.

On p.17 he tries to prove that such an L is directed (filtrant croissant): any x, y have a common strict upper bound. Connectedness gives a zigzag chain x_i >= y_i <= x_{i+1} >= ... from x to y, and he inducts on its length. For length <= 1 (x <= y) one just takes z > y, which exists by regularity. For length n, write x ~_{n-1} z ~_1 y. By induction there is x' > x, z. If z >= y, then x' > x, y and we are done.

This page handles the remaining case z <= y. The diagram shows y > z < x' > x, with a dotted arc and '?' between y and x'. One needs t > x', y. So everything reduces to a 'relative filtration' (local amalgamation / diamond) property: if u < v and u < w, then there exists t with t > v and t > w.

He then crosses out an attempt ('Il ... que visiblement') and observes the following. An order relation that is locally strictly increasing and decreasing, with a' < a < a'' for every a, already defines a model structure of a (connected) regular form: F1-F5 can be checked. But such a structure need not be upward directed, nor dually downward directed. So the desired lemma is false at this level of generality, and the diamond property is a genuinely extra axiom.

On p.19 he gives the counterexample. An ordered set L0 is placed below a family of copies L_i: order inside each piece, and every element of L0 is below every element of every L_i. Two elements of different L_i have no common upper bound. This is the order-theoretic analogue of the branching (non-Hausdorff) line.

Purpose: to decide which axioms on an ordered set make it a faithful model of a 1-dimensional 'forme', for instance whether directedness follows or must be imposed.
errors: The attempted proof (pp.17-18) cannot be completed in the stated generality. The reduction to the diamond property 'u<v, u<w => exists t>v,w' is correct, but that property does not follow from the hypotheses. Grothendieck himself notices this on the page and constructs a counterexample on p.19, so this is a self-corrected gap rather than an uncaught error.
Minor: the case z = y within z <= y is trivial (x' > y already), so only z < y needs the diamond property.

ideas.what: Proving directedness of a connected ordered set by induction on zigzag length, reducing to a local 'diamond' completion property (u<v, u<w => exists t > v,w)
ideas.modern_name: Directedness from local confluence / amalgamation (Newman-lemma-style zigzag argument; 'locally directed implies directed' for connected posets)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore (order theory; cf. confluence arguments in rewriting, Newman 1942)

ideas.what: Locally strictly monotone order with no local extrema, a'<a<a'', as a model of a connected regular 1-dimensional 'forme' satisfying axioms F1-F5
ideas.modern_name: Order-theoretic / combinatorial models of 1-dimensional tame spaces (cf. dense orders, o-minimal or semi-linear 1-dimensional structures)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Unclear; tame topology programme sketched in Esquisse d'un programme (1984)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5-6 sketches 'topologie modérée' only in general terms

ideas.what: Observation that such models need not be upward or downward directed (branching), so directedness is an independent axiom
ideas.modern_name: Branching / non-Hausdorff 1-manifolds (line with branching), trees versus linear orders
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore in topology (branching line, non-Hausdorff manifolds)

missed.claim: Grothendieck's axioms F1-F5 for 'modèles de forme régulière' admit branching (non-directed) ordered models. This suggests his 1986 axiomatics of 'formes' did not exclude non-Hausdorff, tree-like 1-dimensional objects unless directedness ('filtration relative') was added. How the chapter resolves this, whether by adding an axiom or accepting branching forms, is an unexplored detail of his tame-topology programme.
missed.quote: Mais une telle structure n'est pas nécessairement filtrante croissante
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Of mainly historical interest for reconstructing Grothendieck's tame topology axioms. It is mildly relevant to comparisons with o-minimal or semi-linear frameworks, where such branching is excluded.

deep.surprise_reason: An elementary order-theoretic argument with a self-corrected gap and a standard branching counterexample. Interest is only historical, as a window on the axiomatics (F1-F5) of Grothendieck's unpublished 'géométrie des formes'.
transcription_corrections: 'Mais on voit que une relation d'ordre commune' is perhaps 'Mais on note qu'une relation d'ordre ...'; the word after 'ordre' is uncertain.
'de forme régulière connexe[?]': the image reads something like 'de forme[?] ... régulière'; 'connexe' is doubtful.
'(dualis.)' at the end: the image may read '(dualem.)', i.e. 'dualement', meaning not necessarily decreasing-directed either.
'il suffit de trouver [-t-] tel que t > x', y': the crossed-out symbol is a struck 't' (or a struck 'x'); the inequality is t > x', y.
